name: Resonance — Collaborative Neural Music Scene
description: Resonance is an underground music form built around direct BCI-to-BCI musical transmission — performers and audience connect through shared neural protocols to experience music not as sound but as direct sensory and emotional data, bypassing ears entirely. Resonance performances are called 'links' and can only be experienced by participants with compatible BCI configurations, creating an intensely exclusive community. The music itself is composed in neural-notation software and exists in no audible form — it cannot be recorded in any conventional sense, only re-linked. Pioneer composer Adaeze Svensson-Morrow's link series 'Interior Weather' is considered the scene's defining work.
cultural_impact: Resonance has created significant regulatory concern — direct BCI-to-BCI transmission outside corporate-approved protocols is technically illegal under the Meridian Compact's neural sovereignty provisions, making every link a criminal act. The scene has also generated genuine medical debate about the psychological effects of shared emotional transmission.
locations: Link sites (rotating, announced via encrypted Underworld channels)
The Quiet Room (prep space, Tier 2 East)
Adaeze's Studio (location known only to inner circle)
story_hooks: A Resonance link goes wrong and three participants are left in a shared neural loop they cannot exit — the scene's underground protocol engineer is the only person who might be able to break the connection.
Corporate investigators have infiltrated a link site and are building a case — but one of the investigators has experienced Resonance and is now questioning whether to complete the operation.
Adaeze Svensson-Morrow has composed a new link that they claim contains a message from an E.L.F. — the scene is divided between those who believe it and those who think Adaeze has destabilized.
